# E2E Integration Test Pipeline — Plan

## 0. Shape of the thing

Two scenario families (**accept** / **reject**), a pluggable **MarketSelector** + **QuoteStrategy**, a Hedix client fronted by a **safety layer**, and a per-run **artifact bundle**. All orchestrated from `tests/integration/` so the existing `tests/e2e.rs` stays unchanged as the fast in-process suite.

```
rfq-gateway/
├── tests/
│   ├── e2e.rs                       (existing, keep)
│   └── integration/                 (NEW — live Hedix)
│       ├── safety.rs                (rate limit, circuit breaker, budget, dry-run)
│       ├── hedix_client.rs          (typed REST client — goes through safety)
│       ├── market_selector.rs       (trait + default impl)
│       ├── pricing_strategy.rs      (trait + default + ForcedReject)
│       ├── scenarios/
│       │   ├── accept.rs
│       │   └── reject.rs
│       ├── report.rs                (artifact writer)
│       └── harness.rs               (wires selector + strategy + clients)
├── scripts/
│   ├── market-snapshot.sh           (read-only: active markets + orderbooks)
│   └── run-e2e-integration.sh
└── artifacts/{ISO8601-shortsha}/    (gitignored)
```

## 1. Safety layer — built FIRST, before any Hedix network call

All of this is unit-tested with `wiremock-rs` against a fake Hedix — no real calls until step 3 of §8.

| Control | Default | Override |
|---|---|---|
| Token-bucket rate limiter | 5 req/s, burst 10 | `HEDIX_RPS` |
| Circuit breaker | open after 3× 5xx; 30 s cooldown | `HEDIX_CB_*` |
| Request timeout | 3 s per call | `HEDIX_TIMEOUT_MS` |
| Retry | 3×, exp backoff w/ jitter, **only on network/5xx** | `HEDIX_RETRIES` |
| Budget guard | ≤ R$100 collateral per run | `HEDIX_MAX_BRL` |
| Write scope | **OFF by default** — reads only | `--write` flag + `HEDIX_CONFIRM=1` |
| Env gate | staging by default; prod requires `HEDIX_ENV=prod` + `I_KNOW=1` | env |
| Dry-run | logs the request, no send | `--dry-run` |
| Audit log | every HTTP call → `artifacts/.../hedix-calls.jsonl` (key redacted) | always on |
| `client_intent_id` | UUIDv4 per logical op, reused on retry | — |

Rejection of a safety check must **halt the run** (non-zero exit), not skip-and-continue.

## 2. Hedix API primer (what we use & why)

| Endpoint | We use for | Safety note |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/mm/markets` | Discover ACTIVE markets | Throttled; cached 30 s per run |
| `GET /api/mm/markets/{ticker}` | Detail (title, dates, last trade) | Paired with orderbook |
| `GET /api/mm/markets/{ticker}/orderbook` | L2 depth; basis for pricing | Primary read of the cycle |
| `GET /api/mm/balance` | Pre-flight before any write | Abort if `available` < budget |
| `GET /api/mm/positions` | Reconcile after fill | Read-only |
| `POST /api/mm/orders` | Write-path (opt-in only) | Max qty 1, valid_for 30 s |
| `DELETE /api/mm/orders/{id}` | Teardown | Always runs on scenario exit |

Key invariants worth encoding in the client:
- **YES/NO symmetry:** NO bid @ P = YES ask @ (1000 − P).
- **Collateral:** BUY pays `price_cents`; SELL reserves `1000 − price_cents`.
- **Idempotency everywhere** via `client_intent_id`.
- **Batch orders** cap at 2, same market — enforce client-side before the POST.

## 3. Market selection (pluggable)

```rust
trait MarketSelector {
    fn select(&self, client: &HedixClient) -> Result<Vec<SelectedMarket>>;
}
```

Default `LiquidAndNotExpiring`:
1. `GET /markets?limit=100` (paginate).
2. Keep markets with `expiration_date > now + 24h`.
3. For each, `GET /orderbook`; require `best_bid && best_ask && spread ≤ 200 cents`.
4. Sort by tightest spread; take top-N.
5. Emit `SelectedMarket { ticker, best_bid, best_ask, spread, last_trade }`.

Override: `MARKET_TICKER=...` env short-circuits the selector (useful for reruns). Snapshot persisted to `markets.json` so a run can be replayed deterministically.

## 4. Quoting strategy (pluggable)

```rust
trait QuoteStrategy {
    fn price(&self, ticker: &str, side: Side, qty: u64, ob: &Orderbook) -> QuoteDecision;
}
enum QuoteDecision { Quote { price_cents: i32 }, Reject { code: RejectCode, msg: String } }
```

Defaults shipped:
- `MidpointPlusSpread` — `mid ± configured_spread`; rejects if best bid/ask missing.
- `ForcedReject(code)` — test-only; wired via a gateway build flag so it cannot leak to prod.

This is the layer that decides whether the gateway returns 200 or 422. The current `PricingEngine` becomes one impl of this trait; the trait is its extension point.

## 5. User interaction cycles

Actors: **User** (Hedix retail trader, simulated by the test harness posting to Hedix's RFQ flow or directly to our `/api/v1/rfq/quote` depending on lane) → **Hedix** (exchange, in write lanes) → **RFQ Gateway** (us) → back.

### A. Accept cycle (the golden path)

| # | Actor | Action | Expected gateway behavior | Expected response | Expected user-visible output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Harness | Selector picks `SELIC-2026DEC-T15.00` | — | — | Logged in `markets.json` |
| 2 | Harness | Snapshot orderbook + balance | — | — | `accept.jsonl` step=pre |
| 3 | User → Gateway | `POST /api/v1/rfq/quote` `{ticker, side:"yes", qty:1, auto_accept:true, client_intent_id:UUID}` | Validate → selector confirms ACTIVE → strategy returns price from orderbook mid → FSM Active→Accepted → persisted | `200 {status:"accepted", price_cents∈[1,999], fee_cents, filled_price_cents, filled_quantity, accepted_at}` | User sees filled quote |
| 4 | User → Gateway | Same `client_intent_id` again | Store hit | `409 QUOTE_ALREADY_ACCEPTED` | User shown "already filled" |
| 5 | Harness (write lane only) | Mirror fill on Hedix: `POST /api/mm/orders` with echoing `client_intent_id` | — | `201` | — |
| 6 | Harness | `GET /positions` | — | delta ≥ 1 | Artifact: `position.json` |
| 7 | Harness | Teardown: cancel any OPEN orders | — | `200` on each | — |

### B. Reject cycles (four variants, each deterministic)

| Variant | Trigger | Expected gateway behavior | Expected response | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B1 — INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY** | Harness builds gateway with `ForcedReject(INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY)` strategy | Validate OK → strategy returns Reject → **not persisted** | `422 INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY` | Retry with same `client_intent_id` → another `422` (rejects aren't stored) |
| **B2 — MARKET_CLOSED** | Selector fed a ticker whose `status!=active` (or selector stub) | Gateway rejects in market-status check | `422 MARKET_CLOSED` | Same as B1 |
| **B3 — INVALID_QUANTITY** | Harness posts `quantity:0` | Validation short-circuits before strategy | `400 INVALID_QUANTITY` | N/A |
| **B4 — UNAUTHORIZED / FORBIDDEN** | Missing / wrong `X-API-Key` | Auth middleware | `401 UNAUTHORIZED` / `403 FORBIDDEN` | N/A |

**Hard assertion across all B variants:** zero Hedix write calls — verified by diffing the `hedix-calls.jsonl` audit log. Rejection paths must be inert.

*Decision to confirm:* today `QuoteAlreadyAccepted` requires storing rejects. Recommendation: don't store rejects — a rejected quote isn't "accepted" and the client should be free to retry. Matches current `routes/quote.rs` which only inserts on the accept path.

## 6. Artifacts (one bundle per run)

```
artifacts/{ISO8601}-{shortsha}/
├── run.json              (commit, branch, env, strategy IDs, config hash, safety-layer settings)
├── markets.json          (selector output — replay input)
├── accept.jsonl          (one JSON per step: req, resp, latency_ms, assertion results)
├── reject.jsonl          (same for each reject variant)
├── hedix-calls.jsonl     (every Hedix HTTP call, redacted)
├── summary.json          (PASS/FAIL counts + p50/p95 latencies)
└── report.md             (human-readable; extends tests/report.sh format)
```

CI uploads the directory; replay tool takes `markets.json` + `run.json` to rerun deterministically.

## 7. Modular composition rules

- **New quoting strategy** → implement `QuoteStrategy`, register in `harness::strategies()`, no scenario changes.
- **New market universe** → new `MarketSelector` impl.
- **New scenario** → module under `scenarios/`, registered in `scenarios::all()`; picks whatever selector/strategy the harness passes in.
- **New assertion kind** → extend `report::Check` enum; structured so reports render without touching scenarios.
- Config hash in `run.json` makes it obvious when the surface changed between runs.

## 8. Rollout order (each step shippable on its own)

1. `safety.rs` + unit tests with `wiremock-rs`. No net access.
2. `hedix_client.rs` for **reads only**, composed over `safety.rs`.
3. `scripts/market-snapshot.sh` — **first real Hedix call**; staging only. Review its output before proceeding.
4. `MarketSelector` + `QuoteStrategy` traits; port current `PricingEngine` as one impl.
5. Accept scenario (no Hedix writes).
6. Reject scenarios B1–B4.
7. Artifact writer + `run-e2e-integration.sh`.
8. *(Later, behind `--write`)* Write-path mirroring + position reconciliation.
9. `docs/e2e-integration.md` with runbook.

## 9. Decisions I want from you before I start coding

1. **Default env** — staging only by default, prod requires explicit opt-in? (Recommend yes.)
2. **Write lane in v1** — ship read-only first and add writes in a follow-up, or plan both up front? (Recommend read-only first.)
3. **Reject persistence** — confirm rejects should **not** be stored (matches current code).
4. **Budget ceiling** — R$100/run OK, or lower for first real write test?
5. **CI lane** — run integration against `wiremock` in CI + a nightly job against staging?

Confirm those five and I'll open a stacked set of PRs following §8.

# Plan revisions

## §1 Safety — updated defaults

| Control | New value |
|---|---|
| Env default | **staging**; prod requires `HEDIX_ENV=prod` + `I_KNOW=1` |
| Budget guard | **R$1000/run** max reserved collateral |
| Write scope | read + write both in v1 (see §5) |
| CI | none; manual runs only. `scripts/run-e2e-integration.sh` is the entry point |

Budget enforcement is **pre-flight + running-total**: read `GET /balance` at start, track reserved centavos across every `POST /orders` in-process, abort the run before a POST that would breach R$1000 (100 000 centavos).

## §5 Gateway write path (if my interpretation above is correct)

New step inside `POST /api/v1/rfq/quote`, between "strategy prices" and "FSM accept":

```
price → reserve locally → POST Hedix /api/mm/orders with echoed client_intent_id
       ├─ 201/200 ok  → FSM Accept → respond 200 to user
       ├─ 402 INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE → FSM Reject → 422 INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY
       ├─ 409 MARKET_NOT_ACTIVE   → FSM Reject → 422 MARKET_CLOSED
       ├─ 207 partial/mixed       → FSM Reject → 422 + attempt DELETE of any placed leg
       └─ network/5xx after retries → FSM Reject → 502 UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE (new error code)
```

Consequences:
- `client_intent_id` flows through end-to-end: user → gateway → Hedix. Same ID used for the RFQ idempotency check **and** the Hedix order idempotency key. Safe retries, single source of truth.
- New `RfqError::UpstreamUnavailable` (502) for Hedix failures after the safety layer exhausted retries.
- Reject scenarios B1–B4 stay as-is (gateway-local rejects, never reach Hedix). Add **B5 — UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE** driven by `wiremock` returning 503.
- Accept scenario gains an assertion: a Hedix order with matching `client_intent_id` exists (`GET /orders?market_ticker=...`).

## §6 Artifact layout — partitioned interaction log

Replaces the flat `hedix-calls.jsonl`:

```
artifacts/{run_id}/
├── run.json
├── markets.json
├── summary.json
├── report.md
└── interactions/
    └── {source}/{contract}/{endpoint}/{ISO8601Z}-{intent_id}.json
```

- `source` ∈ `hedix`, `gateway`, `user_sim` (who made the call)
- `contract` = market ticker, or `_account` for balance/positions, or `_meta` for health/auth
- `endpoint` = sanitized path (`mm-markets`, `mm-markets-ticker-orderbook`, `rfq-quote`, …)
- Each file:

```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "run_id": "...",
    "ts": "2026-04-15T12:34:56.789Z",
    "source": "hedix",
    "contract": "SELIC-2026DEC-T15.00",
    "endpoint": "mm-markets-ticker-orderbook",
    "method": "GET",
    "status": 200,
    "latency_ms": 42,
    "client_intent_id": "...",
    "correlation_id": "...",
    "safety": { "rate_limited": false, "retries": 0, "circuit_state": "closed" }
  },
  "payload": {
    "request":  { "url": "...", "headers": { "X-API-Key": "***" }, "body": null },
    "response": { "headers": {...}, "body": {...} }
  }
}
```

Design notes:
- Partitioning by `{source}/{contract}/{endpoint}` makes per-market and per-endpoint replays trivial (`find interactions/hedix/SELIC-.../mm-markets-ticker-orderbook -type f`).
- `correlation_id` ties a user request to every downstream call it triggered (gateway → Hedix fan-out), so you can reconstruct one full cycle with one grep.
- Payload is written atomically; metadata is also emitted as one line to `summary/index.jsonl` for fast scanning without walking the tree.
- API keys redacted at write time (`***`), never logged raw.
- The same writer is used by production gateway and by the test harness, controlled by an `InteractionSink` trait — prod defaults to in-memory/no-op, tests point it at `artifacts/`.

## §8 Rollout, revised

1. `safety.rs` (+ `wiremock` unit tests)
2. `InteractionSink` trait + filesystem impl (partitioned writer) — used by everything downstream
3. `hedix_client.rs` read ops, composed over safety + sink
4. `scripts/market-snapshot.sh` — first real staging call
5. `MarketSelector` + `QuoteStrategy` traits; port `PricingEngine`
6. Accept scenario, read-only assertions
7. Reject scenarios B1–B4
8. **Gateway Hedix-write integration** (new step in `routes/quote.rs`), feature-flagged `HEDIX_WRITE_ENABLED`
9. Accept scenario extended: assert mirror Hedix order exists; teardown cancels any OPEN legs
10. Reject scenario B5 — UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE via `wiremock`
11. `docs/e2e-integration.md` runbook

## Versioning path → 0.2.0 stable

Start at `0.2.0-beta.1`. Each substantive PR bumps the beta counter; cut `0.2.0-rc.1` after the write-path lands and integration passes on staging; promote to `0.2.0` once one clean run against staging is archived and a smoke against the pinned prod config is green.

Rule: **no MAJOR bumps while pre-1.0** — breaking API changes within 0.x increment the MINOR (we're already on 0.2). Reserve `1.0.0` for when the gateway has stood up real market-maker traffic without incident for a defined soak period.

## Guardrails that matter more now

Since the one live gateway carries the write path:
- **Feature flag first:** `HEDIX_WRITE_ENABLED=0` is the default in Fly until PR #8 is merged *and* one clean read-only integration run is archived. PR #8 lands with the flag still `0`; a separate `fly secrets set` flips it — no code deploy to enable writes.

- **Kill switch:** `HEDIX_WRITE_ENABLED=0` must be honored mid-request — checked right before the Hedix `POST /orders`, not just at startup. Flipping the secret + `flyctl machine restart` is the abort procedure.

# PR #4 — Bundled: Harness foundations (beta.5)

Rationale: the script alone is small, but it's also the moment we first hit real staging Hedix. Worth bundling with the abstractions that the scenarios need, so the extension points are in place when we get there.

## Bundle scope

| Piece | File(s) | Why in this bundle |
|---|---|---|
| Pagination helper | `src/hedix/client.rs` — `list_markets_all(filters, max_pages)` | Needed by the script; trivial on top of existing `list_markets` |
| `MarketSelector` trait + default | `src/strategies/market_selector.rs` | Extension point #1 for scenarios; script uses it |
| `QuoteStrategy` trait + two impls | `src/strategies/quote_strategy.rs` (`MidpointPlusSpread`, `ForcedReject`) | Extension point #2; `PricingEngine` becomes one impl |
| `run_id` generator | `src/runtime.rs` — `RunId::new()` → `{ISO8601Z}-{short-sha}-{hostname}` | Shared by script and later harness |
| `rfq-snapshot` binary | `src/bin/rfq_snapshot.rs` | Reads env, builds client with `FsSink`, calls `list_markets_all` + `get_orderbook` for top N, writes `markets.json` |
| Script wrapper | `scripts/market-snapshot.sh` | Sets `HEDIX_ENV`, `HEDIX_BASE_URL`, calls binary, prints artifact path |
| `.gitignore` | add `artifacts/` | Local runs shouldn't commit output |
| Docs stub | `docs/e2e-integration.md` — runbook skeleton with staging-only warning | First docs touch; will grow each PR |

What's **not** in this bundle:
- No scenarios yet (PR #5)
- No gateway routing changes (`routes/quote.rs` untouched)
- No write path (PR #6)
- Existing `PricingEngine` stays where it is; `QuoteStrategy` trait exists alongside, will absorb it in PR #6

Version bump: **`0.2.0-beta.5`**. New public library API (`list_markets_all`, two traits, `RunId`) warrants a beta counter bump even though there's no breaking change.

First-run story: user runs `scripts/market-snapshot.sh` against the already-deployed Fly gateway's Hedix config (via the binary hitting staging directly, using `HEDIX_BASE_URL`). Artifacts drop into `artifacts/{run_id}/`. We review the output before shipping anything else.

| # | Bundle | Beta | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | **Harness foundations** (this one) | `0.2.0-beta.5` | script + traits + pagination; first real staging read |
| 5 | **Accept + reject scenarios B1–B4** | `0.2.0-beta.6` | `tests/integration/` scenarios + report writer; all gateway-local (no Hedix writes) |

| 7 | **Reconciliation + B5 upstream + docs** | `0.2.0-beta.8` | Accept scenario asserts mirror order via `GET /orders`; B5 via wiremock; `docs/e2e-integration.md` completed |

Five more PRs. Pace feels right — each one ships a discrete capability and each beta is independently runnable and useful.

**Risk flags for the path:**

## Assistant · 2026-04-16T01:12:33

Reading the spec carefully revealed an important architectural point. Let me spell out the **correct** flow per `api/rfq-api.yaml` v2.0.0, and flag a concern about PR #6.

# RFQ user flow — per spec

## The one-line summary

> User places order on Hedix → Hedix has no counter-party → Hedix fans out RFQs to all configured MMs in parallel → each MM response becomes an order Hedix places in its own book to match against the user.

The MM (us) **does not place its own order**. Hedix creates the MM's counter-order from the RFQ response body. Our only job is: receive the RFQ, price it, return an accepted quote fast.

Source: `api/rfq-api.yaml:5-13`:
> "Hedix requests quotes from configured market makers when an order has no counterparty in the order book. Quotes are requested from all MMs in parallel (fan-out); **each response becomes an independent order in the book.**"

And line 16-17:
> "Hedix then uses the accepted quote to create a counter-order in the order book."

## Full sequence — happy path

| # | Actor | Action | System state | What the user sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **User** | Opens a market (e.g. `COPOM-2027MAY01-T15.00`) on Hedix, selects "Buy YES", qty 10, submits | User's intent registered at Hedix | Market page, order ticket |
| 2 | **Hedix** | Looks for a SELL YES counter-party @ acceptable price in the order book | No match found | Spinner / "finding liquidity" |
| 3 | **Hedix** | Generates a `client_intent_id` (UUID tied to this user order). Fans out RFQ in parallel to every configured MM | Multiple in-flight HTTP calls | Still spinning |
| 4a | **Hedix → us** | `POST /api/v1/rfq/quote` with `{ticker, side=yes, quantity=10, auto_accept=true, client_intent_id=<uuid>}` | Request in flight | — |
| 4b | **Our gateway** | Validates → idempotency check → `QuoteStrategy.price(...)` → returns 200 with `{quote_id, price_cents, status=accepted, filled_price_cents, filled_quantity, fee_cents, valid_for_seconds, accepted_at}` | Quote persisted (intent_id → quote) | — |
| 5 | **Hedix** | Collects responses from all MMs | Best-quote selection | — |
| 6 | **Hedix** | **Creates an MM counter-order in its book** (at the accepted price, for our quantity, TTL = `valid_for_seconds`). One counter-order per winning RFQ response | MM counter-order = OPEN, user order still pending | Still spinning |
| 7 | **Hedix matching engine** | Matches user's BUY YES against the MM's SELL YES counter-order | User order FILLED, MM order FILLED | — |
| 8 | **Hedix** | Settles the trade, updates both sides' positions | User has +10 YES, MM has -10 YES (or +10 NO cover) | **"Filled 10 × YES @ R$5.00 (R$50 total)"** |
| 9 | **User** | Sees fill receipt | Done | Position tile updated on Hedix |
| 10 | **MM** (us, out of band) | `GET /api/mm/positions` (periodic polling) | Sees new -10 YES position on COPOM-2027MAY01-T15.00 | — |

## Where our gateway lives in the flow

**Only step 4b.** A single stateless responder. Sub-100ms budget. No outbound calls to Hedix during the RFQ response — Hedix handles order placement on the book itself from our response shape.

## Reject paths — what the user experiences

| Our response | Hedix behavior | User outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `422 MARKET_CLOSED` | Our MM excluded from this RFQ round | If another MM accepted → user fills; if all MMs reject → Hedix returns "no liquidity" |
| `422 INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY` | Same | Same |
| `400 INVALID_QUANTITY` | Treated as MM error; we're flagged | Same — user sees "no liquidity" unless another MM covers |
| `409 QUOTE_ALREADY_ACCEPTED` | Idempotent replay — Hedix gets back the already-accepted quote | User sees normal fill |
| `410 QUOTE_EXPIRED` | RFQ round too slow | User sees retry or "no liquidity" |
| `429 RATE_LIMITED` | Our MM skipped this round | Same as `422` — other MMs cover |
| timeout / no response | Same as reject — we're excluded | Same |

Per-MM rejects aren't user-fatal: Hedix fans out to all MMs, so as long as one responds accepted, the user fills.

## 🚩 PR #6 concern — we may have built the wrong thing

Our `v0.3.0` puts `POST /api/mm/orders` inside the RFQ handler: when `HEDIX_WRITE_ENABLED=1`, the gateway fires a second HTTP call to Hedix to place a SELL order before returning 200. Per the spec above, **that's redundant** — Hedix already creates the counter-order from our RFQ response body. We'd be double-booking.

Reading `api/mm-api.yaml` more carefully, `POST /api/mm/orders` is for **proactive, two-sided market making** (posting resting orders *before* user demand arrives, independent of RFQs). Spec confirms it: `"Use case: Two-sided liquidity provision — submit SELL YES + SELL NO in one call"` (`api/mm-api.yaml:233`). That's a separate workflow from RFQ.

So:
- For the RFQ flow (what Hedix actually calls us for), `v0.2.0` is the correct shape. Stateless, read-only from our side. `0.2.0` already does this.
- `0.3.0`'s write path is useful for proactive market making — a future "post resting quotes at these prices" feature — but it doesn't belong inside the RFQ handler.
- The practical reason `v0.3.0` is safe today: Hedix hasn't shipped `POST /api/mm/orders`, so the feature is unreachable. But once they do, flipping the flag could cause double-orders for every user quote we win.

## Recommendation

Keep `HEDIX_WRITE_ENABLED=0` **permanently** for the RFQ flow. The flag's current design wires `POST /api/mm/orders` into the RFQ response path, which is a misread of the spec.

Three options:

1. **Minimal fix:** leave the code, document `HEDIX_WRITE_ENABLED=1` as "do not enable for the RFQ-only flow". Ship a note in `docs/e2e-integration.md`. Next feature PR removes the mirror call from the RFQ path and moves it to a dedicated proactive-MM path.
2. **Correct fix in `0.3.1`:** remove the mirror call from `routes/quote.rs`. `POST /api/mm/orders` support stays in `HedixClient` (it's useful) but only callable from a future proactive-MM scheduler, never from the RFQ handler.
3. **Revert to `0.2.0` behavior in production via flag:** no code change, just policy.

Want me to do option 2 as `0.3.1` so the write path isn't sitting in the RFQ handler waiting to misfire when Hedix deploys?

## Market-specific expected behavior (concrete picks)

| Market | Last trade | Our quote @ 500c | Spread vs last | User outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `COPOM-2027MAY01-T15.00` | 507c | 500c | -7c (we sell cheap) | Filled, user saves 7c/contract |
| `COPOM-2027MAY01-T14.25` | 445c | 500c | +55c | User's buy @ ≤500c from us — if another MM quotes 446c, Hedix picks that, we lose |
| `COPOM-2027MAY01-T15.25` | 555c | 500c | -55c | We sell way below market — great for user, bad for us |
| `BTC31MAR-2027MAR01-T90000` | 50c | 500c | +450c | **We'd reject in practice** — quoting 500c on a 5% probability contract is nonsense. But `PlaceholderStrategy` has no sanity check |

Placeholder pricing means the gateway is **economically unsafe** for any market whose true value is far from 500c. Two ways to fix:
1. Tighten `RFQ_PLACEHOLDER_PRICE_CENTS` per-market (doesn't scale)
2. Plug in `MidpointPlusSpread` strategy — but that needs an orderbook, and staging orderbooks 404

Before the first real user order, decide which markets we're willing to quote on. A safe default might be: **only quote on markets where our strategy can produce an informed price**. The gateway should call `GET /api/mm/markets/{ticker}` + `get_orderbook(...)` per RFQ and reject if the book is unusable (empty or wildly inconsistent with 500c).

1. **Ticker allow-list.** Add `RFQ_TICKER_ALLOWLIST` env var. If set, the gateway rejects any RFQ for a ticker not on the list. Default: unset = allow all (current behavior). For the first test user, set it to `COPOM-2027MAY01-T15.00` only. Small, safe, reversible.
2. **Guard against nonsense pricing.** Add an optional `max_placeholder_deviation_cents` — if the ticker has a `last_trade_price_cents` (via pre-flight `GET /api/mm/markets/{ticker}`) that's more than N cents away from our placeholder, reject with `INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY`. Protects us from the BTC-T90000 case above.

Both are 30-minute PRs, defensive, no BREAKING. Would ship as `0.3.1`.

## Assistant · 2026-04-16T09:43:28

Core clarification: **no, we do not call `POST /api/mm/orders` in the RFQ flow.** The spec is clear: `rfq-api.yaml:11` says *"each response becomes an independent order in the book"* — Hedix creates the book order from our response body, we don't place one ourselves.

Proof by elimination: Hedix staging returns 404 on `POST /api/mm/orders`. If the RFQ flow required it, staging RFQs would be impossible. The endpoint belongs to a separate "proactive market making" workflow, not RFQ.

## What happens after we return `200 accepted`

### Scenario A — match (happy path)

```
Us:    200 {status: "accepted", price_cents: 500, filled_quantity: 1, valid_for_seconds: 300}
        ↓
Hedix: creates SELL YES order in book under our MM account at {500c, qty=1, TTL=300s}
        ↓
Hedix matcher: user's BUY YES qty=1 matches against our SELL YES qty=1 at 500c
        ↓
Both sides fill atomically → trade created → settlement
        ↓
User:  sees "Filled 1 × SIM @ R$5,00"
Our position on Hedix:  −1 YES on COPOM-2027MAY01-T15.00  (visible via GET /api/mm/positions)
Our MemoryStore:        quote_id marked accepted, client_intent_id indexed
```

**Our reconciliation:** periodic `GET /api/mm/positions` confirms Hedix agrees we're short 1 YES. If match counts agree, we're settled.

### Scenario B — we returned accepted, but no match

Possible causes, in decreasing likelihood:

| Cause | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Another MM offered a tighter price.** Hedix fans out to all MMs in parallel; user order fills against cheapest. Our SELL order sits as a resting offer in the book. | Our SELL rests on book → TTL 300s → expires → auto-cancel. No position change on Hedix. |
| **User cancelled before match.** User's BUY order pulled between RFQ fan-out and matching. | Same as above: our SELL rests, expires on TTL. |
| **Valid-for-seconds too short / race.** Our TTL expires before matcher gets to us. | Order expires unmatched. |
| **Partial fill.** Our quote was qty=10 but user only wanted qty=3. 3 fill, 7 rest, 7 eventually expire. | Partial position: `−3 YES` on Hedix, `−7` resting until TTL. |
| **Hedix error / race with another accept.** Rare; Hedix-side issue. | Depends on Hedix's handling. |

In all no-match cases:

```
Us:               MemoryStore shows quote_id = accepted
Hedix book:       resting SELL order under our account at our price, TTL 300s
After TTL:        Hedix auto-cancels the resting order
Our position:     unchanged (no fill happened)
Our MemoryStore:  still shows accepted — MISMATCH with reality
```

**This is a real reconciliation problem.** Our current `QuoteFSM` doesn't distinguish "accepted and filled" from "accepted but resting-and-expired".

### What reconciliation would look like

We don't have it implemented yet. Options for a future `0.4.0`:

1. **Poll `GET /api/mm/positions`** every N seconds; compare against our accepted quotes' expected positions. Flag mismatches.
2. **Poll `GET /api/mm/orders?status=CANCELLED`** (once Hedix deploys it); any order with a `client_intent_id` matching one of our accepted quotes + `cancellation_reason=EXPIRED` means no-match.
3. **Hedix webhook / notification** if they add one (spec doesn't describe one today).

For the first user order — this is fine to defer. Staging has no deployed write or orders-list endpoint anyway. The reconciliation gap only bites once volume picks up.

Updating the Hedix doc now to call this out.
